view: Consensus (six-member mean): 2w 35/27/38, this quarter 34/31/35, next quarter 42/23/35 (up/range/down). Every member also has buying paused or set to Wait. The six forecasts sit within 2-5 points of each other because they share inputs: all six add 14-20 points to 2w down for the same SEC headline and the same close-at-the-low bar, and all six cut range for the same 8.5% ATR. That is one piece of evidence counted six times, not six confirmations. I lean slightly against the down tilt (2w 38/28/34) and more against it at 13 weeks (45/22/33). I agree that no ladder should be active while TB2 stands. A ladder draft is fine if it stays dormant, opens on events rather than prices, and is not built on ATH-anchored fibs, crash-inflated ATR spacing or analyst EPS.

probabilities.defs: 2w +/-5%, quarters +/-10%, vs price_at_call 125.53 (Fri 2026-11-20 close, weekend run). next_2_weeks: up = close > 131.81, down = close < 119.25, range between; measured at the close on or before 2026-12-06 (Fri 2026-12-04). this_quarter: last close of 2026-12-31; next_quarter: last close of 2027-03-31; up = close > 138.08, down = close < 112.98, range between. up + range + down = 100.

consensus.line: Mean of six: 2w 35/27/38, this quarter 34/31/35, next quarter 42/23/35. All tactical stances are Wait or Avoid New Entry, and TB2 is treated as standing. Quarter-down estimates span only 32-36 across six lanes whose confidence runs from 30 to 44.

opposite_case.point: The outside view is 33/45/22, with up larger than down. Using only the unconditional touch rates, 2w +5% is reached in 52.2% of windows and -5% in 41.2% (reachability.windows.2w). The engine gives 50.2% for a touch of 131.81 by 2026-12-04 and 39.6% for 119.25. On the closing measure, the consensus puts down (38) above up (35) and close to the unconditional -5% touch rate. Turning the base-rate skew around needs strong lane-specific evidence. In the submissions, the down shift comes from one governance headline and one bar.

Every conditional table points the same way. After 2w drops of 15% or more: 2w 50/50/0, 13w 100/0/0, median +32.1% (n=4). After weekly RSI <= 36: 13w 69/0/31, median +21.5% (n=13). These are weak, overlapping samples and I do not lean on them. But a 0% down outcome is still evidence against 2w down at 38-42, and the consensus has discounted them to near zero.

The business evidence is the opposite of the price action. Revenue was $115.84B (+103% YoY, 6.5% above estimate) and the Q4 guide of $130B is 4.2% above consensus even with zero China data-center revenue assumed. Gross margin was 74.9%. Hyperscaler capex is rising: 0 of 4 falling, run-rate vs TTM +15.9% to +43.6% (hyperscaler_capex). The bear case needs the reported numbers to be wrong, and that rests on a press report, not a filing.

The SEC item is a Reuters report from two people briefed that enforcement staff are 'examining potential accounting issues'. Nvidia did not respond and the SEC declined to comment. No subpoena, Wells notice, restatement or company disclosure is in the slice. WSJ had already reported an SEC investigation on 2026-11-17, and NVDA fell for four sessions after that, so part of Friday's -14% re-priced a story the market already knew. The narrative member's own draft TB5 says a press report should not fire it.

Most of Friday's move was sector-wide: NVDA -14.01% vs SOX -10.73% and AMD -13.25%, an NVDA-specific excess of about 3.3 points. For the week the gap was about 5.8 points vs SOX (relative.this_week_nvda_minus_sox_pts). With beta to SPX of 1.94 (relative.beta_vs_spx_59w), a market rebound from a VIX of 35.9 (tv_purple_list.vix) moves NVDA roughly twice as far. The consensus attributes the down tilt to the SEC story, but the sector explains most of the price move.

HY OAS is 3.52 (+0.05) and NFCI is -0.48, so this is equity fear without credit stress. AAII bears were already at 51.4 before the crash week, with a one-year high of 53.3 (sentiment_aaii, stale). Broad fear without a credit event is the setting in which oversold mega-caps rebound. The macro member says so and still puts quarter down at 34.

The bearish reading of the closing bar is one session's close location, cited by technical, sentiment, relative_strength, narrative and fundamentals. A bar that closes 0.8% above its low after an afternoon headline (price_note: Reuters report in the afternoon) says little about the next day. It is n=1, and the same members note that the Nov 12 reversal bar also failed (also n=1).

hunt.point: SMALL SAMPLES. n=4 overlapping windows are about one episode (the technical member says so), and the n=13 RSI table is autocorrelated. The members handle them correctly as weak evidence. Several also use n=1 analogies as patterns, none with a sample: 'worst week since Oct 2008', 'Nov 12 reversal failed so volume does not mark lows', 'single-name governance shocks keep underperforming' (relative_strength, judgment) and 'high VIX usually mean-reverts' (macro, not in slice). The chair should give these zero weight on both sides.

DOUBLE COUNTING. (a) The range cut: all six cut 2w range by 16-20 points for the same ATR of 10.71 (8.5%). That ATR includes Friday's 19.2-point bar (143.725 to 124.50), so it is crash-inflated, and part of the cut belongs to a volatility regime that may not last 10 sessions. One cut, counted once, is right; a range near 28 is defensible, but below 25 is not. (b) The down shift: the SEC headline (governance group) adds +14 to +20 to down in every lane, including macro ('SEC/accounting tail, outside my lane') and relative_strength. Under the shared rules the governance group counts once. Averaging six lanes that all priced it in counts it six times. (c) Weekly RSI 25, Stoch RSI 0/0, daily RSI 15 and MACD are one momentum group. Technical and sentiment flag this correctly; the chair should not add the oversold rebound argument again from relative_strength or macro.

ANALYST TARGETS. Fundamentals correctly discounts the 242.79 average and 222.5 median. The same analyst group comes back in through a different door: forward P/E 8.4 and the derived forward EPS of 14.94 are consensus estimates (fwd_pe_note cites Motley Fool and CNBC), and 'FY28 estimates up ~23% in 90 days' (news_governance) was set before the SEC report. Fundamentals' ladder levels (149.4 = 10x forward, 112.1 = 7.5x forward) are analyst EPS multiplied by a chosen multiple. If the SEC question is real, E is the uncertain input, so these levels are circular. The only multiple not built on analysts is the one on reported EPS (2.68 x 4), and that is the figure under question.

UNREAD PAGES THE CONSENSUS DEPENDS ON. (1) sec_filings is partial: the Q3 10-Q has not been located and its legal-proceedings section is unread. The whole down tilt and the proposed TB5 depend on what the SEC matter is, and the one document that might say so is unread. Re-read it before the chair rules. (2) options_positioning is deferred. Without implied move, skew and dealer gamma, nobody can say whether the 124-120 zone has a put wall (support) or short gamma (an accelerant). The consensus treats this gap as symmetric, but it is unknown in both directions. (3) The AAII and CNN pages date from before the crash. ADX and peer weekly data are missing. Six members at confidence 30-44 producing nearly the same numbers on 7/14 ok pages shows shared gaps, not agreement.

ATH ANCHORING. Linear fibs run from 10.81 to the 243.37 ATH, and the log 0.786 (124.98) uses the same anchors. Technical's 'four-way confluence' at 122-127 is linear fib 0.5 + log fib 0.786 (one ATH anchor, two scales) + Friday's low 124.50 (the current price, not an independent support) + the 200W SMA 124.14. Only the 200W SMA is independent, so it is a one-way confluence. N3 97-100 (fib 0.382) is ATH-derived too, with the swing at 97.40 as the only independent leg, yet it gets the largest weight (3.0). Sentiment's 'half off the high' audit applies to the ladder as well as to the forecasts.

ANCHORING TO THE PROPOSED LADDER. The members repeat 'price is inside L4' as if the zone meant something. L4 (124-128) was set on 2026-11-11 from the 200W SMA and fib 0.5 and was never approved. The week of 2026-11-16 traded 163.20 to 124.50, through all four zones. Had the ladder been live, it would have filled 100% of budget in one week at an average of 139.99, about 10.3% above the 125.53 close. That is the lesson to log: a price-only ladder spaced 4.8-13.5% apart cannot survive an information shock. Technical's N1 keeps L4 almost unchanged (122-127) at 73.8% touch by 2026-12-04. A rung that fills 'almost surely if placed' is a market order, not a ladder level.

EARNINGS AS A PREDICTABLE EVENT, and an unpriced TB3 size. Before the print, fundamentals and narrative said a beat-and-raise would support the stock. It beat and the stock fell 10.4% in three sessions. The members now record that lesson. The opposite mistake now is treating the late-Feb 2027 print (inside next_quarter) as the clearing event for the accounting question; it is a binary event like the last one. On TB3, fundamentals sizes China exposure at $2.4B (2.1% of revenue). The new rule also requires licences for Singapore and Malaysia, and the FT reports Singapore-billed sales near half of revenue (news_governance). Billing location is not end use, and the slice gives no at-risk figure. Both '2.1%' and 'half of revenue' are unsupported as measures of TB3 materiality. The Q4 guide came a day after the rule was filed, and whether it reflects the rule is not in the slice.

A smaller miss: fundamentals says a full loss on the $118B of guarantees 'would not explain the drawdown' (about $4.9/share). The same slice carries BofA's estimate of $230B total guarantees (news_governance). Neither figure is confirmed. The point holds only on the company's number.

evidence.point: Outside view 33/45/22. My 2w: 38/28/34 (up +5, range -17, down +12). I take one ATR-based range cut (range 28, not 25) and one governance shift to down (+12, counted once). I keep up above the base because the -32.7% two-week move, VIX 35.9 and beta 1.94 make a reflex bounce of 5% (a partial retrace of a -14% day) at least as likely as a further 5% close lower. Against the consensus: up +3, down -4.

Base 39/43/18 becomes 37/30/33. 138.08 sits below the 143.725-145.71 gap, and the engine puts touch odds at 52.7% for 138.08 and 36.4% for 112.98 by 2026-12-31. FOMC 2026-12-09 and CPI 2026-12-10 (fcst 3.9) add two-sided variance. The governance follow-ons (testimony requested 12-01/12-03, possible 8-K) add down. Against the consensus: up +3, down -2.

Base 50/31/19 becomes 45/22/33. The consensus took up down by 8 and down up by 16. I take up down by 5 and down up by 14. Over 13 weeks the reported revenue, the guide, rising capex and an 8.4x forward multiple (built on consensus EPS, so only partly independent) favour up unless the numbers are impaired. Impairment is not yet evidenced by any filing, but it is possible, and the late-Feb print is a second binary. That is why down stays well above base.

Whether any ladder should be active: no. TB2 was FIRED by the chair on 2026-11-12, the owner has not confirmed it, and the approved rule says any one break pauses all buying. TB3 is a candidate: on wording it meets the narrative member's pre-committed test, but materiality is unquantified. The SEC report is not a thesis break. Until the owner rules on TB2/TB3, a new ladder can only be a dormant draft. The red-team caveat: if the owner rejects TB2, and TB3 proves immaterial, the only thing left against buying is a press report, which the members' own draft TB5 classes as WATCH. Stacking TB2, TB3 and a draft TB5 with no dated un-pause tests risks the pre-mortem both fundamentals and narrative wrote: missing the low at about 8x earnings.

Rule L audit for the chair: L1 162-164, L2 154-157, L3 141-145 and L4 124-128 are all 'resting (proposed)'. None was approved or placed and filled_orders is empty. All four zones traded during the paused week of 2026-11-16. Record L1-L3 as 'passed during TB2 pause, dropped' and L4 as 'in zone at call, paused', never as fills. No row is removed.

ladder_critique: Activation: keep any updated ladder dormant until TB2 and TB3 are ruled on. Gate activation on dated events, not prices: (a) the Q3 10-Q is found and read (legal proceedings, any SEC disclosure, guarantee footnote) by 2026-12-04; (b) the 12-01 to 12-03 sessions (if held) produce no credible report that Nvidia knew of diversion; (c) the owner rules on TB3 materiality by the about 2027-02-17 licence deadline. 'A permanent CEO is named' (narrative) has no date in the slice, so it is not a usable gate on its own.

Urgency: sentiment's advice is right. Do not finalise a ladder this weekend. Write the dormant draft now as a pre-commitment, but do not activate anything before at least the 11-23 to 11-25 sessions (technical's trap clock) and the 10-Q read. Technical's N1 at 73.8% touch by 12-04 and its 3.5 of 8.5 dip weight 'likely to trade before 12-31' would put the most money to work in the period when the SEC, testimony and TB3 overhangs are least resolved.

ATR spacing: technical's 10-12% spacing (1.2-1.4 ATR) uses an ATR of 10.71 that includes a 19.2-point crash day. When volatility falls, those rungs will be about 2 ATR apart and may never fill. Set spacing in percent from the structure, not in units of the crash ATR. N2 110-114 has no structural anchor (technical says so), so it should carry the least weight or be dropped, not get 1.5.

Anchors: count only independent anchors. The 200W SMA 124.14 (rising weekly) and the swing labels 97.40, 90.69 and 86.62 are independent. Fibs from 243.37 are tie-breakers. On that basis N1 is a single-anchor level and N3 a two-anchor level, and the 3.0 weight at N3 (fib 0.382) is anchoring dressed as confluence.

Independent gates are better than price: relative_strength's 'NVDA/SOX no new low for two weekly closes' and macro's 'no more than about a third of remaining weight before FOMC/CPI 12-09/10' use evidence that is not momentum and not governance. Fundamentals' 'credibility tranche' released by a clean filing is the right idea. Its EPS-multiple levels are not, because they use the analyst E that the SEC question puts in doubt.
Technical's conversion of L3 into a confirmation tranche (daily close above 145.71) is sound and avoids catching a broken trend. Engine reach for 143.725 by 2026-12-04 is 10.6% (reachable).

key_levels.why: 200W SMA, the only independent anchor in the 122-128 cluster. Technical's trap rule: a close below that is reclaimed within 1-3 closes is bullish; two closes below 122 is a confirmed break. Engine: 124.14 by 2026-11-25 46.2%; 122 28.7%.
2w up line. A close above it before 2026-12-04 means the governance-driven down tilt was overcounted (engine touch 50.2%).
2w down line (engine touch 39.6% by 2026-12-04). A close below it while SOX holds up means the consensus was right to add the SEC discount.
NVDA/SOX ratio now. This separates the two stories: a sector washout (ratio holds or rises) vs an NVDA-specific accounting discount (new lows).
Bottom of the SEC-day gap. A fill means the accounting headline was priced as process (engine 10.6% by 12-04).

checks.check: Close location vs the 200W SMA in the first three sessions, by the 2026-11-25 close. Two or more closes below 122 with no reclaim of 124.14 favours the consensus down tilt. A close below 124.14 reclaimed within 1-3 closes, or any close above 131.81, favours the red team.

Company disclosure on the SEC matter. Find and read the Q3 FY27 10-Q (legal proceedings, any SEC inquiry or subpoena language, guarantee footnote) or any 8-K. Words like 'subpoena', 'formal investigation' or 'Wells', or a delayed filing, favour the consensus. Silence or 'informal inquiry' with clean financial statements favours the red team.

NVDA/SOX weekly ratio at the 2026-11-27 and 2026-12-04 closes. New lows below 14.93 in a SOX bounce mean an NVDA-specific accounting discount, which favours the consensus. Two weekly readings without a new low mean a sector washout that the consensus over-attributed to the SEC story, which favours the red team.

what_would_change_my_mind: Toward the consensus or more bearish: two or more consecutive daily closes below 122 by 2026-12-04 without a reclaim of 124.14 (engine: 122 by 11-25 28.7%; technical: 57.1% by 12-04). I would move 2w to about 33/25/42.

Toward the consensus: Nvidia confirms a formal SEC investigation, subpoena or Wells notice, or delays its 10-Q, by 2026-12-04. Next quarter down to about 40 or higher, and I would support a WATCH under the draft TB5.
Toward my view: a daily close above 131.81 by 2026-12-04 (engine 50.2%) while NVDA/SOX holds at or above 14.93. 2w up to about 45.
Toward my view: the Q3 10-Q is found and contains no SEC-inquiry or legal-proceedings language on accounting, by 2026-12-04. Next quarter up to about 50.

TB3 materiality: a company or BIS figure for revenue at risk under the remote-access rule, before about 2027-02-17. A figure near the FT's 'about half of revenue billed in Singapore' would move next quarter down above 40 whatever the price does.
Expected (not triggers): the weekly closes of 11-27 and 12-04, the ex-dividend date 12-02, FOMC 12-09, CPI 12-10 and the late-Feb print will all happen. Only their outcomes count.
notes_for_chair: Weighting: do not average the six. They share one governance input and one ATR input. Take each lane's independent evidence only. Macro: VIX/credit/Fed calendar. Relative strength: NVDA/SOX. Sentiment: volume and stale surveys. Technical: levels and trap clock. Fundamentals: reported numbers vs guarantees. Narrative: TB rulings. Apply the SEC shift once.
Re-read sec_filings (10-Q legal proceedings) before ruling. It is the unread page the whole down tilt depends on.
Options positioning is deferred: the 120-125 zone could hold a put wall or short gamma. Treat it as unknown in both directions, not as neutral.

Lessons-log candidate: a price-only ladder (L1-L4, gaps 4.8-13.5%) would have filled 100% of weight within one week at an average of 139.99 during the TB2 pause. Ladders need event gates and percent spacing wider than one shock day.

Pre-mortem (consensus): three months on, the committee was badly wrong because six lanes priced the same Reuters headline six times, the SEC matter proved narrow, and an 8x-forward stock with rising hyperscaler capex re-rated through 138.08 while every ladder stayed paused on stacked TB2/TB3/TB5 gates with no dated un-pause test. Pre-mortem (mine): the 10-Q or testimony confirmed a revenue-attribution problem on the Singapore channel, forward E was cut, and my up tilt leaned on beta and n=4 tables.
